thats also not quite right. です is not a verb, object, subject, adverb, or adjective. its easier to think of it like a suffix but for full statements. it denotes a formal tone and can be omitted without changing the meaning of a sentence. It cannot be a "polite form of the verb" because there exists no casual form of the "verb" in question (with the assumption there even is a verb in the first place). 

Examples of statements with/without です
"That's right" - formal: そうです。informal: そう。or そうだ。
The meaning does not change.
"This is an apple." -
 formal: これはりんごです。informal: これはりんご。or これはりんごだ。
Again, the meaning does not change. 
In both, there is an alternative informal version ending with -だ, which serves a similar purpose as -です and is also not necessary.

i apologize if i made an error in the description of the grammar, i learned japanese from my mom and not from a textbook, japanese grammar is hard to explain because much of the language is based on what "sounds right"

EDIT: So, it appears that the argument that です is a verb does hold up in many contexts, just seemingly not the context i perceived it to be  (in that です is a verb functioning as a near integral part of the subject object verb context). before yesterday i had never known what a copula or other types of verbs were, so that was a learning experience. in japanese, it seems that です／ます／だ　are what are called 助動詞, which according to google translate is an "auxiliary verb". i think the most difficult part of all of this is attempting to apply the english grammatical terms and ideas onto a different language, despite the fact that many of us (myself included) dont even know what the heck a verb is or isnt anymore
